facts.label: Passado simples: acidente
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para contar o que aconteceu: I fell, I hurt my ankle. Pergunte com Did + verbo base e negue com didn’t.

facts.label: Passado irregular
facts.sub: Muitos verbos mudam no passado: fall, fell; hurt, hurt; get, got; see, saw; put, put. Decore os mais usados: I fell off my bike. Verbos irregulares não terminam em -ed.

facts.label: Did + verbo base
facts.sub: Nas perguntas, use Did + sujeito + verbo base: Did you hit your head? Did it hurt? Não use o passado depois de did. A resposta curta é Yes, I did ou No, I didn’t.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The past of fall is fell.
We say “I falled off my bike.”
items.why: Say I fell off my bike.

items.s: Did you hit your head? is a past question.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The past of fall is fell. → Verdadeiro (I fell off my bike.)
We say “I falled off my bike.” → Falso (Say I fell off my bike.)
Did you hit your head? is a past question. → Verdadeiro (Did + base verb.)

pages.title: A park by a lake in Melbourne · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Saturday in Melbourne. Paulo rode his bike in the park. He went fast near the lake. A dog ran across the path. Dirk saw the accident from a bench. He ran to help his friend.
“Paulo! I saw you on the ground. What happened?” says Dirk. “I fell off my bike near the lake. A dog ran across the path.” says Paulo. “Did you hit your head? Where did it hurt?” says Dirk.
